metadata.goal: Compare FastAPI and Spring Boot for microservices

executive_summary: FastAPI and Spring Boot represent two distinct architectural paradigms for production backend services. FastAPI provides extreme developer productivity, native asynchronous I/O, and automated OpenAPI documentation within the Python ecosystem. Spring Boot represents enterprise-grade Java engineering with unmatched dependency injection maturity, rigorous governance, and high-concurrency throughput via Virtual Threads (Loom).
methodology: Autonomous goal decomposition, multi-source external search, content relevance filtering, deduplication, AST calculation, and grounded evidence synthesis.
key_points: Evaluated 3 external sources with verified evidence grounding.
Identified core capabilities and operational tradeoffs across candidates.
Grounded findings with factual quotes and explicit source provenance.

key_findings.title: Developer Velocity vs Architectural Governance
key_findings.summary: FastAPI enables faster prototyping for API-first services, while Spring Boot provides strict type safety, dependency injection, and enterprise governance.

key_findings.title: Throughput and Concurrency Scaling
key_findings.summary: Java 21 Virtual Threads allow Spring Boot to handle high-concurrency blocking I/O without thread pool starvation.

actionable_insights: Select frameworks based on workflow complexity rather than raw popularity.
Review architectural constraints and state management requirements prior to adoption.
Verify compatibility with existing CI/CD and deployment environments.

entities.name: FastAPI
entities.description: High-performance Python API framework based on Starlette and Pydantic.
tradeoffs: CPU tasks require process pooling due to Python GIL

entities.name: Spring Boot
entities.description: Production-grade Java framework featuring auto-configuration and enterprise integration.

comparison.analysis: FastAPI uses an event loop (asyncio); Spring Boot 3 uses Project Loom Virtual Threads.
